title: Rav Huna bar Acha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni, he reports a teaching in R’ Alexandri’s name [1]. Hyman also lists him in aggadic passages in Shemot Rabbah 43:4, Vayikra Rabbah 1:3, Kohelet Rabbah 5:7, Midrash Shmuel 26:4, and Midrash Tehillim 18:9.

notes.text: The source duplicates ר׳ before Alexandri; it is translated once, with marker [1] retained. The Midrash Shmuel section label ר remains unresolved.

The saved whole Krakow1893 MidrashShmuel26 scalar3 explicitly has abbreviated R' Huna bar Acha, corresponding to26:4. Supplied פ״כו־ר remains alongside that match, not a proved printed dalet-to-resh error. Full Rav in the supplied heading is retained without harmonizing the other edition’s abbreviation. Alexandri’s duplicate ר׳ is rendered once with [1] preserved; neither a full personal title nor the missing footnote is newly established. All other aggadic references and the MaaserSheni citation remain uninspected in this wake.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 347) reads Midrash Shmuel 26:4, where the Krakow edition mentions R’ Huna bar Acha. Hyman repeats the title before Alexandri across a line break. The supplied transcription adds [1], whose content has not been established. In Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 5:5, Rabbi Huna bar Acha transmits a teaching in Rabbi Alexandra’s name. Shemot Rabbah 43:4 and Vayikra Rabbah 1:3 also name him. The cited Kohelet Rabbah and Midrash Tehillim references retain Hyman’s attribution.
